source: US Dam Hazard Classification - Corrected Edition (2026-11-09), Appendix A; In-Depth Summaries: Dam & Pond Hazard Classification - Federal Agencies and the States (Nov. 2026)

S1.name: Sunny-day failure at normal pool
S1.starting_condition: Normal pool (lowest ungated spillway crest or typical operating level)
S1.source: Common baseline; New York and Virginia name it explicitly

S2.name: Sunny-day failure, reservoir full to high water line
S2.starting_condition: Emergency spillway crest, or dam crest if none
S2.source: Colorado; Rhode Island uses top of embankment for new and currently-Low dams

S3.name: Top of dam or PMF peak, whichever is lower
S3.starting_condition: Water at the top of dam or the PMF peak, whichever is lower; no added inflow; no coincident downstream flooding
S3.breach_assumption: Piping failure or TR-60 peak discharge (REG_05.2026 § 5.1.1, per the Summaries S-9)

S4.name: Peak pool during 100-year flood routing
S4.starting_condition: Peak pool during routing of the 100-year flood, never below the auxiliary spillway crest; no coincident downstream flooding
S4.source: Nebraska Classification of Dams (Dec. 2023) §§ 2.32, 2.35 (confirmed in the Dec. 2023 edition, Summaries S-7)

S5.name: Flood plus failure (rainy day)
S5.starting_condition: SDF or PMF with failure versus the same flood without failure; count only the incremental rise
S5.source: New York (rainy-day run); Virginia (SDF with and without failure and PMF with failure)

S6.name: Scenario set by current class
S6.starting_condition: New or Low -> S2 at top of embankment; existing High -> 1/2 PMF; existing Significant -> 500-year storm

S7.name: Multiple breach locations along an above-grade impoundment
S7.starting_condition: Several breach locations; most severe governs

D1.name: Incremental rise cutoff
D1.rule: stop where incremental rise falls to about 2 ft or less

D2.name: Water-surface convergence cutoff
D2.rule: stop where breach and non-breach water surfaces converge within 1 ft

dam_fields_note: 'a|b' means either field satisfies the need. Missing fields are flagged by preflight, never silently passed.
assumptions: Bridges and culverts work as designed and are not blocked by debris (New York).
Spillway-sizing hazard (e.g. Colorado's Hydrologic Hazard) is outside classification.
